links.outcome: Clinical quality (relevance, accuracy, balance, scope) and non-clinical quality (empathy, understandability, readability) of patient-education answers on thyroid eye disease
links.effect: Clinical mean score 5.55 for ChatGPT-RAG vs 4.94 for ChatGPT. ChatGPT-RAG was intermediate overall, trailing ChatGPT on non-clinical metrics (g = 0.44) and trailing OpenEvidence clinically (g = 0.53).
links.tradeoff: The RAG model scored lower than plain ChatGPT on non-clinical metrics (empathy, understandability, actionability).
links.quote: Across both domains, ChatGPT-RAG achieved intermediate performance, more closely trailing OpenEvidence clinically (g = 0.53) and ChatGPT with respect to non-clinical metrics (g = 0.44).

links.comparator_used: General-purpose ChatGPT (GPT-4o-mini) and the ChatGPT-RAG model
links.outcome: Clinical ratings (accuracy, relevance and others) versus non-clinical ratings (empathy, understandability, actionability)
links.effect: Clinical mean score 5.96 for OpenEvidence vs 4.94 for ChatGPT (Hedges' g = 1.21, P < 0.001) and vs 5.55 for ChatGPT-RAG (g = 0.53, P < 0.001). On non-clinical metrics ChatGPT scored 18.4 vs 14.96 for OpenEvidence (g = 1.25, P < 0.001).
links.tradeoff: The medicine-specific model scored worse on empathy, understandability and actionability than the general-purpose model.
links.quote: OpenEvidence significantly outperformed both ChatGPT (mean clinical score 5.96 vs 4.94; Hedges' g = 1.21, P < 0.001) and ChatGPT-RAG (5.96 vs 5.55; g = 0.53, P < 0.001) in clinical rankings and across most clinical metrics, including accuracy and relevance.

design_hint: retrieval grounding (RAG) added to a general-purpose chatbot
